subject: Rebaseline: POC scope and success criteria — ACME
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmecorp.com>, Jing Li <jing.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — ACME POC

Hi Carlos & Jing,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great discussion and really excited about running a short POC with Acme. Quick recap and suggested next steps (please correct me if I missed anything):

- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference for customer-facing summarization + internal support-routing use case.
- Success criteria (initial):
  - Summarization: avg ROUGE-L >= 0.55 vs. Acme in-house baseline on the 200 test prompts
  - Latency: 95th pct latency <= 600ms for 512-token JVM-sized requests under 1 RPS ramp; target 200ms for cache-hit patterns
  - Cost: <$0.03 per 1k tokens served at expected QPS when batching enabled
  - Reliability: <1% error rate over 1 week of runs
- Timeline: 4-week hands-on POC (kickoff next week), with week 1: infra & data onboarding; week 2-3: evaluation runs; week 4: wrap + findings
- Owners: Marissa (commercial), Rishi (SE lead), Jing & Carlos (customer success & data owner)

I've attached the draft POC scope (acme-poc-scope-v1.xlsx) and a quick evaluation plan (acme-poc-metrics.xlsx).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm success criteria and whether we should add any additional KPIs (e.g., user satisfaction surveys).
2) Confirm kickoff date (we suggested Mon Aug 3).
3) Provide access for Rishi to a small sample of data (S3 link or files) and indicate any redaction requirements.

If you want to add the internal support triage use case we briefly mentioned, that’s fine — we can rebaseline the success criteria to include intent-classification F1 targets. If you want that included, please flag so we can update timing/effort.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: acme-poc-scope-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: acme-poc-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — ACME POC

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Mostly looks good. A couple of updates from our side: 

- We definitely want the internal support triage use case included. That’s actually higher priority than the external summarization for our rollout path. Key success criteria for triage: intent-classification F1 >= 0.78 (on our labeled sample – I can share a CSV) and routing accuracy >= 85% to the correct team queue.
- Can we extend the POC to 5 weeks? Our data team has a couple of downstream commitments next week so they may not be fully available during week 1.
- Kickoff: Aug 5 would be better for us (Wed) but we can be flexible if you need earlier.

We’ll upload a ~2k-row labeled sample to the S3 bucket and share creds with Rishi. I’ll also include a short doc that describes our current routing rules.

Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
carlos.mendez@acmecorp.com

Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — ACME POC

Hi all,

Thanks Carlos for the note — adding the triage use case is fine but a couple of items to call out from an SE perspective: 

- Data & labeling: a 2k-row labeled sample is perfect for evaluating intent F1. Please include label schema and examples of ambiguous cases.
- Metrics: I suggest we split evaluation metrics by use case. Proposed updated success criteria: 
  - Summarization: avg ROUGE-L >= 0.55 on the 200 prompt set (unchanged)
  - Triage (intent classification): micro F1 >= 0.78 on the 2k sample; routing accuracy >= 85% on a 500 holdout test set
  - Latency: 95th pct <= 700ms once we include the triage pipeline (slightly relaxed given extra context handling)
  - Stability: no more than 2 production-like outages during the 5-week run

- Infrastructure: we can run the initial evaluation on a small dedicated pool (p2.xlarge equivalent). If results look good, we’ll suggest a throughput profile for dedicated capacity.

- Timeline/effort: because of the added triage use case and Carlos’s request to shift kickoff to Aug 5, we should rebaseline to 5 weeks. I’ll update the evaluation plan to show which tests we’ll run each week and what artifacts you should expect.

I’ve sketched changes into the POC doc and will share a revised spreadsheet (acme-poc-scope-v2.xlsx) by end of day.

Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Updated POC scope & sign-off request — ACME (v2)

Hi Carlos & team,

Thanks for the quick responses. Attached is acme-poc-scope-v2.xlsx which reflects the updated scope (5-week POC, added triage use case) and revised success criteria per Rishi's recommendations. High-level changes: 

- POC length: 5 weeks, kickoff Wed Aug 5 (customer preference)
- Added triage use case with F1 and routing accuracy targets.
- Latency target relaxed to 95th <= 700ms to account for additional context.
- SE scheduling: Rishi will lead evaluation; we will provide weekly checkpoints and a mid-point demo in week 3.
- Commercial: Dev flagged potential change-order for SE effort; we will treat week 6 as optional paid validation unless we roll it into a paid pilot.

Please reply with a brief sign-off (can be a single line) so we can lock resources and confirm the kickoff calendar invite. If you want to tweak any criteria, flag those now — this will be the baseline we use for acceptance at the end of the POC.

Thanks,
Marissa
